findings.title: Certified Pre-Owned: Abusing Active Directory Certificate Services
findings.summary_md: SpecterOps researchers Will Schroeder and Lee Christensen published the Certified Pre-Owned research identifying AD CS misconfiguration classes ESC1 through ESC8, including ESC1 template abuse that lets a low-privileged requester obtain a certificate for a privileged account and ESC8 NTLM relay to AD CS web enrollment endpoints. They reported the ESC8 relay issue to MSRC on May 19, 2021 and MSRC responded on June 8, 2021 that it was valid but did not meet the bar for a security update, directing customers to enable Extended Protection for Authentication. The research notes ESC1-ESC7 elevation issues were already proliferating in real environments since January 2021.

findings.title: New PetitPotam attack allows take over of Windows domains
findings.summary_md: French security researcher Gilles Lionel (topotam) disclosed PetitPotam on July 18, 2021 and released a proof-of-concept that forces a Windows server to authenticate to an attacker-controlled system via the MS-EFSRPC EfsRpcOpenFileRaw function. Security researcher Remi Escourrou noted the combo of PetitPotam with PKI ESC8 is especially effective, enabling network access to full AD takeover. Microsoft published advisory KB5005413 on mitigating NTLM relay attacks against AD CS in response.

findings.title: Microsoft Releases Guidance for Mitigating PetitPotam NTLM Relay Attacks
findings.summary_md: CISA alerted administrators that Microsoft released KB5005413 on July 23, 2021 to address the PetitPotam NTLM relay attack against Active Directory Certificate Services. The advisory instructs customers to review KB5005413 and apply the necessary mitigations such as disabling NTLM on AD CS web enrollment endpoints and enabling Extended Protection for Authentication. The mitigations target relay of coerced machine-account authentication to certificate enrollment services.

findings.title: Cross-tenant helpdesk impersonation to data exfiltration: A human-operated intrusion playbook
findings.summary_md: Microsoft documented a human-operated intrusion playbook in which attackers initiate cross-tenant Microsoft Teams communications while impersonating IT or help desk personnel to socially engineer users into granting remote access via Quick Assist. From that foothold, operators used trusted vendor-signed runtimes, native administrative protocols such as WinRM, and Rclone to move laterally and stage business data for exfiltration to external cloud storage. This earlier playbook established the same social-engineering and remote-access pattern later seen in the ESC1 and ESC8 certificate-abuse intrusions.
